styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Markets, museums and Swahili city life.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Indian Ocean swims and sunset dhow trips.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Street grills, spice markets and coastal cooking.

stays.why: Walk to markets, the ferry and DART buses. Best base for a short first visit.
Quiet waterfront near the ferry to Kigamboni and the fish market. Good for early starts.
Restaurants, cafés and malls close by; a short ride to the beaches.
Seafront hotels and calm evenings. Popular with business travellers and couples.

food: Try Swahili coastal dishes: pilau rice, urojo soup and grilled fish with coconut.
Mchikichini and Kariakoo markets are good for spices, fruit and cheap local meals.
Seafood is best near the water: Msasani and Oyster Bay have many fish restaurants.
Street food is cheap: mishkaki skewers and chips mayai often cost under TSh 5,000.
Tap water is not for drinking. Stick to bottled or filtered water, even in hotels.
more_time: Take the Kivukoni ferry to Kigamboni for a cheap half-day across the harbour.
Add a boat trip to Bongoyo or Mbudya island for a beach day; check boat times on the day.
History fans can swap a city afternoon for Bagamoyo's old town and slave-trade sites up the coast.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the markets, the waterfront and a beach or island day without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: hot and humid with about 15 rain days. Pack a light rain jacket.
Feb: warm with fewer showers, around 12 rain days. Good for the city.
Mar: rainy spells return, about 20 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
Apr: the wettest month, around 26 rain days. Expect heavy downpours.
May: rain eases to about 16 days and it is slightly cooler.
Jun: drier and cooler, about 8 rain days. A comfortable month.
Jul: the driest, coolest month. Great for walking and beaches.
Aug: dry with about 9 rain days. Pleasant evenings.
Sep: warming up, about 11 rain days. Still a good time to visit.
Oct: hotter with about 14 rain days. Start early to beat the heat.
Nov: short rains begin, around 20 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
Dec: hot and wet, about 21 rain days. Book indoor options too.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical coastal climate: hot all year, with a long rainy season around April and short rains late in the year.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Driest and coolest months, with highs near 28–29°C and few rain days. Ideal for beaches and walking.

items.title: Long rains in April
items.text: About 26 rain days, the wettest month. Expect heavy showers and plan indoor sights.

items.title: Short rains in November and December
items.text: Around 20–21 rain days. Showers are often short but frequent; carry an umbrella.

items.title: Hot and humid all year
items.text: Highs stay around 28–31°C and lows 22–26°C. Drink water and take midday breaks.

items.title: Sea breezes help
items.text: Coastal spots like Oyster Bay and the islands feel cooler than the city centre.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a hat, sunscreen and insect repellent. Add a rain jacket for April and November–December.

transit.best: Ride apps or taxis for most trips; DART buses for cheap cross-city runs.

modes.text: No metro. DART is a bus rapid transit system, not rail.
DART buses run on dedicated lanes; Phase 1 links Kimara to Kivukoni Ferry via Posta. Daladala minibuses are cheap (under TSh 1,000) but slow and crowded; look for POSTA signs.
Taxis are everywhere; agree the fare first, as meters are rare. Bolt and Uber work in Dar and often beat street-taxi prices.
Driving is on the left. Traffic is heavy, especially at evening rush hour.
Walking suits the compact centre. Cycling is possible but risky on busy roads.
Ferries from Kivukoni cross to Kigamboni in the south.
